title: Tenor trombone
reference_instrument: University of Iowa MIS tenor trombone (model and player are stated as NA on the page)
summary: A tenor trombone with the slide in first position, played by a lip valve whose pitch is never an input: the note is the lock the loop finds between the lip and the bore. The bore is the 14-element template Braden (2006) fitted to a measured Conn 88H large-bore tenor, with the bell as four Bessel horns expanded into cones on their exact curves. The lip is the outward-striking mode of the artificial latex lips Cullen (2000) measured, with the mouthpiece volume of the same rig. This lip does not speak at the published mf mouth pressures, so each hold's pressure is read from the model's own threshold, and the tightest setting sits under its threshold and dies away after the attack. The graded sound is the radiated pressure of the actual bell disk at a baffled point 1.524 m away, not the mouthpiece pressure. Nothing was fitted to the Iowa recordings, and the lip setting that gives each note is read from the render, not set from a pitch. It is a population stand-in (a different trombone from the recorded one), and the first stretch of the bore, the mouthpiece and leadpipe, is read off the thesis figure (digitized, with an estimated uncertainty) because the table prints only its end radii.
physics_present: fs-couple brass_loop: a one-degree-of-freedom outward-striking lip island advanced by exact held-force propagation, a Bernoulli aperture solved implicitly with the mouthpiece cup junction, closing on the bore's reflectance

fs-duct multimodal transfer-matrix bore with exact Bessel viscothermal loss, realized as a passive causal line by a convergence ladder over the line length, terminated in the flanged-piston radiation load
the bell as Bessel horns r = b (x0 - s)^-flare through the published end radii and flares, expanded into cones lying exactly on the curve (pieces per horn is a refinement axis)

an outlet observer built from the same duct: the mouth volume flow per incident wave from the same transfer-matrix chain, differentiated and delayed by the Rayleigh integral over the real bell disk to a baffled receiver, so the graded sound is radiated pressure, not mouthpiece pressure
a lip tension gesture (pre-stress) and a blowing-pressure gesture on the shared canonical schedule format, with the held-note and tension-sweep recipes in render.sh
physics_missing: a full account of moving the reflection to the junction's own sample: at 7132 Pa the trombone reads +22.86 cents and +7.02 dB against the 6 kPa card it replaces, its lip gap goes from 0.241 to 0.000 mm, it closes for 38 to 44 percent of the cycle and its bore AC rises 5.30 dB, which is the same note name but not the same state, and not the same note fixed. The +4.49 cents left between the nonlinear and linear bore has no cause, so nothing measured on the nonlinear bore counts for or against gas nonlinearity, the cards stay linear and pexfp.252 stays stopped. The predictions made before these cards rendered missed: trumpet Bb3 read -0.4 cents against +6 and F4 +13.2 against +22, and the pre-stresses landed at 0.93, 1.401, 1.843 and 2.341 against 0.925, 1.392, 1.860 and 2.364 predicted

the mouthpiece and leadpipe as a measured part: element 1 of the bore is digitized from Braden's Figure 5.3 (a scan, with the axes calibrated from the frame ticks and checked against the printed element length and end radii), so its radii carry about 0.015 cm and its axial positions about 0.3 cm of estimated uncertainty, and its cup holds about 9.5 ml give or take 1.5 ml; it is not a measured table, and its first 0.6 cm (the rim) is not resolved
the recorded trombone: the Iowa page gives no model, so the Conn 88H template is a population stand-in and the F attachment is absent

a player's lips: the lip is an artificial latex lip pair on a trombone-size mouthpiece, only its outward-striking mode, with no inward-striking mode; human outward resonances are far lower and more heavily damped, and no human lip mass, width or rest gap is published

a clock that reaches the bell's radiation ceiling: the flanged radiation load is admitted only to ka 20, so the render runs on a 19.2 kHz clock (not 48 kHz) and everything above the receiver's resolved band is unmodelled

a radiation observer resolved across the trombone band: the Rayleigh disk quadrature admits only about 3.9 kHz for this bell, and the mouth-flow transfer is the plane-mode image of the duct, not the multimodal one the reflectance line uses
the microphone: on-axis point source geometry only; the player's bell orientation, the cardioid KM 84 directivity and any room are not modelled

breath-warmed and humidified bore gas, wall vibration, nonlinear propagation and shock formation at forte (the source of brassiness), mutes, slide positions beyond the first, and the slide's own acoustic leakage
a same-specimen impedance pair, so the passive chain is checked only against published population data
